voice.name: en-GB-SoniaNeural
voice.prosody: A father locked his daughter away in the middle of the sea to save her from her fate. Legend says a king was told that his daughter would die from a snake bite on her eighteenth birthday. To save her, he built a tower on this tiny island in the sea and sent her to live there. For years she was safe. On her birthday her father sent her a basket of fruit, but a snake was hidden inside, and the prophecy came true. That is the story behind the name. Another legend tells of a young man who swam across the Bosphorus every night to reach the girl he loved. Its real history is just as long. Over the centuries the tower served as a lighthouse, a lookout and a customs post. It collapsed, burned and was rebuilt many times. Today you can take a boat out and visit, or watch it from the Salacak shore. The tower has appeared in films, including a James Bond film. But the people who understand it best are the locals who sit in Salacak in the evening, drinking tea as the tower's lights come on.
